title: Efficiency publication-ingestion register
description: Boundary schema for the efficiency publication-ingestion register. The register binds every stable-facing surface that describes low-power or thermal behavior -- documentation pages, in-product help, the About surface, service-health, the policy-or-admin surface, and support exports -- to the one canonical efficiency-state claim entry it renders, so each surface points at the same entry instead of cloning low-power prose. The canonical entries are the rows of the M5 efficiency-state governance matrix. Each binding carries the export-safe projection (efficiency state, source-of-change, posture, published ceiling, narrowed effective posture, certification state, claim-support level, override posture, recovery state, and fired narrowing reasons) the surface must render verbatim from the entry, so a narrowed or unsupported claim propagates to every surface in the same train. Raw energy, power, thermal, or battery telemetry, raw provider payloads, raw logs, user content, file paths, machine labels, and secret material never cross this boundary; only stable governance tokens and reviewable sentences do.

reviewable_sentence.description: Short product-term sentence safe for product copy, docs, About, service-health, admin, support export, and release evidence. Raw telemetry, raw provider payloads, raw logs, user content, file paths, machine labels, and secret material MUST NOT appear.

claim_level.description: Ordered low-power claim strength, shared verbatim with the M5 efficiency-state governance matrix.

certification_state.description: Certification outcome of the claim entry, shared verbatim with the governance matrix.

claim_support.description: Whether the published claim is fully supported, narrowed below its ceiling, or unsupported (quarantined). Derived from the entry's certification state and propagated to every consuming surface.

override_posture.description: Whether and how the adaptation may be overridden, shared verbatim with the efficiency governance vocabulary.

recovery_state.description: Recovery state of the adaptation, shared verbatim with the efficiency governance vocabulary.

surface.description: Consuming surface kind. docs is published documentation; help is in-product help; about is the in-product About surface; service_health is the service-health surface; admin is the policy-or-admin surface; support_export is a support or diagnostics export.

requires_claim_bearing.description: Whether a binding to this surface is authorized only for an entry whose effective posture is claim-bearing. The About surface advertises only claim-bearing postures, so it is authorized only for claim-bearing entries.

always_required.description: Whether every entry must be rendered on this surface. Coverage fails when an always-required surface has no binding for an entry.

rendered_projection.description: The values a consuming surface renders for the entry. Every value MUST equal the canonical entry's value so a narrowed or unsupported claim propagates to the surface unchanged.

surface_locator.description: Where the consuming surface renders this entry, e.g. a docs path with an anchor, a help topic id, an About section id, a service-health row id, an admin field-group id, or a support-export field-group id.

consumes_entry_id.description: The governance-matrix row id this surface renders.

renders_verbatim_from_entry.description: Asserts the surface renders the entry's canonical values rather than hand-written low-power prose. The validator requires this to be true.

disclosed_fields.description: The export-safe field names this surface discloses. Every name MUST be in the register's export_safe_fields allowlist and none may be in the forbidden_fields denylist.

narrowed_entry_ids.description: Entries whose effective posture is below their published ceiling; every consuming surface must render the narrowed posture and narrowed claim-support.

quarantined_entry_ids.description: Entries whose certification state is quarantined; every consuming surface must render the unsupported claim, not a stale ceiling.
